business_ops.order_book_absence_evidence: The order_book key is deliberately OMITTED because the document NOWHERE DISCLOSES an order book - this is an absence of disclosure, and is NOT a statement by the issuer that it has none. Verified by exhaustive sweep of the staged full text (1,132,628 chars, all 26 sections): the phrases 'order book', 'orders in hand', 'order in hand', 'outstanding orders', 'unexecuted', 'backlog', 'letter of intent' and 'LOI' return ZERO matches. All 87 occurrences of order/orders/ordering/orderly were individually inspected and every one is either (a) generic prose about customer purchase orders being amendable or cancellable, repeat orders, or quality-driven order cancellation risk; (b) the company's OWN capital-expenditure purchase orders for machinery ('We have considered the above quotations for the budgetary estimate purpose and have not placed orders for them'), which belong to objects_execution and are not forward customer revenue; (c) statutory or judicial 'orders' (SEBI orders, court orders, Standing Orders Act, rectification order u/s 154, refund orders); or (d) IPO application-process boilerplate. The strongest forward-revenue-adjacent statements the document makes are qualitative only: 'we have secured orders from our renowned customers in the past', 'During the last 3 years we have received repeat orders from about 142 number of customers', and 'we have sales and marketing team and business development team that is dedicated to taking new orders' - none carries a value, a date, or an unexecuted percentage. The company also explicitly states it 'typically do[es] not enter into long-term agreements' with customers, which is consistent with there being no contracted forward book to disclose.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: NOT backward integrated into polymer production. The company buys its base resins (LLDPE, HDPE) and functional additives (colour masterbatches, Plasblak, antistatic agents, flame retardants, blowing agents for foam, UV stabilizers, antioxidants) from third-party suppliers - 'primarily sourced from third party suppliers in India', with imports in fiscal 2026 from Canada, Malaysia, Thailand and UK. It holds no long-term supply contracts or fixed-price agreements with any raw material supplier and 'typically source[s] raw materials from the open market', leaving it fully exposed to polymer price volatility with no stated hedge; the single largest supplier accounted for more than 50% of purchases in each of the last three fiscals (62.60% / 64.57% / 61.30%). Restated financials break raw materials consumed into Granules 3,858.35 lakhs, Master Batch 330.08 lakhs and Chemical 94.03 lakhs for FY26 - the dominant input is bought-in polymer granules. Within its own gate the company is integrated across the compound process chain: raw material selection, weighing/batching, compounding (twin-screw or single-screw extrusion) or dry blending, cooling and pelletizing, grinding/pulverizing to a 20-35 mesh target, in-house testing and quality control (MFI, particle size, colour consistency) and packing in 25 kg woven bags - all at one site with its own laboratory and QC department. It is PARTIALLY FORWARD integrated one step past the compound: it also moulds finished custom moulded tanks (water, fuel, chemical) on three rotational moulding machines, and sells rotolining and toll pulverising job-work services to the same industry it supplies compounds to. On the sales side it states it 'sell[s] directly to majority of our customers' in a B2B model (the document does not describe the channel for the remaining minority, and no distribution or agency network of its own is disclosed), while simultaneously acting as the inbound all-India distributor for four foreign principals (Lysis Technologies UK, Axel Plastics USA, 493K Ltd Northern Ireland, Salee Colour Plc Thailand), which is a lateral trading extension rather than integration. Utilities are partly captive: 177 kWp rooftop solar supplements Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Co. Ltd. grid supply, water comes from an on-site borewell, and the plant is a zero liquid discharge facility with cooling towers and an RO system. The site itself is LEASED, not owned. The company states it has no collaborations, tie-ups or joint ventures other than in the normal course of business.

The arithmetic only works if the exceptional item is a CREDIT, which is how Annexure-AC prints it (Total -3.50, being Loss by Fire 77.48 less Insurance Claim 80.98). The P&L drops the negative sign and its '(V-VI)' label contradicts its own arithmetic.

contradictions.detail: The RHP defines EBITDA as PBT + Depreciation + Interest Expenses - Other Income, and elsewhere reports Finance Costs of 104.62 / 88.23 / 62.44. Substituting the finance cost line does not reproduce the printed EBITDA in any year. Only the Annexure-Z 'Interest Expense' sub-total (103.50 / 86.50 / 60.95, excluding 'Other Borrowing Costs — Others Charges') reproduces it. This is a definitional trap rather than a numeric error, but a downstream recomputation using finance cost will disagree with the printed EBITDA by 1.13 / 1.73 / 1.49.

return_ratios_notes.definitions_as_printed: RoNW = restated PAT / net worth at the END of the year. RoE = net profit after tax / AVERAGE shareholders' equity — which is why RoE exceeds RoNW in FY2026 and FY2025 but is HIGHER than RoNW in FY2024 as well (28.18 vs 24.70). RoCE = EBIT / capital employed, capital employed = net worth + total debt + lease liabilities + deferred tax.

market_position.basis: The RHP states no market share for the Company and provides no industry-comparison table. Positioning is stated qualitatively: the Company is 'engaged in the manufacturing of rotational molding (roto molding) compounds, which serve as a key raw material for producing a wide range of hollow plastic products through the rotational molding process', supplying 'customized polyethylene-based compounds, formulated using Linear Low-Density Polyethylene (LLDPE), High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE), and other specialty additives' in powder or granulated form. The issuer states under 'Basis for Offer Price' that 'There are no listed companies in India that is engaged in only in the business of manufacturing of rotational molding (roto molding) compounds', and describes a single manufacturing facility at Gat No-172, Khatwad, Tal - Dindori, Dist - Nashik, Maharashtra of approximately 5,100 sq. mts. with 33 permanent employees as on June 30, 2026. It is ISO 9001:2015 certified, recognised as a One Star Export House by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, a member of The Plastics Export Promotion Council (PLEXCONCIL), and as of March 31, 2026 its product portfolio is sold in around 21 countries and in 24 states in India. The Company describes its competitive field as 'various large and small manufactures that develop similar products that we sell' and states 'We compete with various companies in organised and unorganised structure.' The RHP makes no claim of market leadership, rank or share.

industry_peers.no_peer_note: The issuer affirmatively states it has no comparable listed peer, in two places within 'Basis for Offer Price' (Section: objects). (1) Under '5. Comparison of Accounting Ratios with Industry Peers:' — "There are no listed companies in India that are engaged in a business similar to that of our company accordingly it is not possible to provide an industry comparison in relation to our company." (2) Under '7. Set forth below are the details of comparison of key performance of indicators with our listed industry peers:' — "There are no listed companies in India that is engaged in only in the business of manufacturing of rotational molding (roto molding) compounds . Accordingly, it is not possible to provide a comparison of key performance indicators of industry with our Company." Consequently the RHP prints no peer-comparison table and no peer P/E, EPS, NAV, RoNW or total income figures; the P/E ratio table at item 2 is left as [bullet] placeholders pending the Price Band, and the industry P/E block that would normally accompany a peer set is absent rather than blank.

Raw material price volatility and availability: raw materials are sourced from third party suppliers in India and imported from Thailand, Malaysia and the UK; the absence of long-term fixed-price contracts exposes the Company to price volatility that it may be unable to pass on to customers.

Export and geopolitical risk: revenue from exports was Rs. 1,316.78 lakhs, Rs. 1,418.82 lakhs and Rs. 1,456.91 lakhs in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, constituting 23.32%, 28.21% and 31.02% of revenue from operations; the RHP specifically flags exposure to Iraq (geopolitical instability, regulatory uncertainty, dependence of the Iraqi economy on crude oil exports) and the risk of tariffs, quotas and other trade barriers.

Exchange rate fluctuation risk, unhedged, on both export receipts and imported raw materials (imports of raw materials were Rs. 232.12 lakhs, Rs. 62.24 lakhs and Rs. 167.15 lakhs in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024).

Environmental and plastics regulation: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) Regulations for plastic packaging mandating minimum reuse, recycling and recycled content, bans on certain single-use plastics, and the Hazardous Waste Management Rules.
Technology risk: the RHP states it cannot assure that technology developed by others will not render its products less competitive or attractive.

Capacity utilisation risk: utilisation is affected by raw material availability and industry and market conditions, and the RHP states that failure to achieve full capacity utilisation would result in operational inefficiencies.

The logo used by the Company is currently under process of registration under the Trade Marks Act, 1999.
Small employee base: 33 permanent employees as on June 30, 2026.

overview.business_model: Three revenue streams, all disclosed in the Our Business chapter and in ₹ lakhs as printed.
